newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP copper half profit down 32 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP copper half profit down 32 pct.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Friday profits from its copper division were A$217 million in the six months to November 30, down 32.2 percent on the corresponding period last year.
BHP said in a statement accompanying its half-year results that copper results were affected by lower average realised copper prices, including unfavourable settlement adjustments.

Higher despatches from the Escondida copper-gold project in Chile, lower despatches from the Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea and "the unfavourable but improving" results from the North American division also affected the result, BHP said.
BHP produces nearly one million tonnes of copper a year, making it the world's second largest copper company.
Copper prices were sent into a tailspin in June after Sumitomo Corp of Japan revealed huge losses from copper trades.
Copper prices have since recovered to around US$2,155 a tonne from a 1996 low of around US$1,745.
However, some analysts expect production of copper to outpace demand next year, which threatens to place further downside pressure on price.
Profit from the copper division for the November quarter was A$132 million, compared to A$85 million for the August 1996 quarter.

Partial recovery of copper prices during the month of November, increased despatches from Ok Tedi and Escondida and lower costs in the North America and Metals divisions contributed to the improved result, BHP said.
Unhedged copper shipments not finalised as of November 30, 1996 have been brought to account at US$1.00 a pound, the company said.

For the remainder of the financial year ending May 31, 1997, 43 percent of anticipated shipments are covered by put options at US 95 cents a pound and nine percent by forward contracts at US$1.02 a pound, BHP said.
Depreciation an amortisation charges increased by A$119 million to A$180 million, BHP said.
The rise reflects the acquisition of Magma Copper Co and the commissioning of a new plant in Chile, it said.
Exploration costs were A$37 million for the half-year, up from A$26 million in the same period a year ago, BHP said.
